recommendations.summary: Editing plan Closed Decisions busts every task's agent-call cache, forcing a full re-verification pass for a one-line documentation fix.
recommendations.evidence: 5 resumes, 3 triggered purely by plan-amendment edits (7b8684a, 19bca30, 23c4c9b), each costing a full 11-task redo (~1-1.9M tokens, 15-55 min)

recommendations.summary: plan-alignment deviation IDs are non-deterministic LLM slugs, so acceptRisk exact-match can't reliably target the same recurring deviation across resumes.
recommendations.evidence: Same deviation named run-plan-mjs-gatefindings-fix, then execute-plan-gatefindings-fix, then run-plan-mjs-gate-fix across 3 resumes

recommendations.summary: gateFindings() threw on any open finding instead of only critical/major, contradicting the disposition rubric's WARN semantics. Fixed locally; needs upstreaming to savviety-skills.
Cross-check every library named in a plan's Closed Decisions actually appears in the scaffolding task's dependency list.
recommendations.evidence: Task 1 named FastAPI/httpx/uvicorn/watchdog as stack choices but never added them as pyproject.toml dependencies, blocking Task 9 (commit 051db5b fixed it)

recommendations.summary: Cross-check every test file implied by an acceptance bullet (e.g. -k <slice>) has a matching write_scope entry.
recommendations.evidence: Tasks 6/7/8 acceptance named unit-test slices whose files were never declared in write_scope (commit 23c4c9b fixed it)

recommendations.summary: A task redone after an unrelated cache-bust may rewrite a file widely enough to clobber an earlier review-fix commit's change to the same file.
recommendations.evidence: kb-ask timeout finding fixed twice across two resumes (7e6f6e1 then 8819480) despite the first fix being an ancestor commit

headline: Editing plan Closed Decisions busts every task's agent-call cache, turning a one-line documentation fix into a full re-verification pass — this was the single biggest cost driver across this run's 5 resumes.
